prompts.text: Name a part of the human head

items.quip: This tiny brain structure takes its name from the Latin for “little rein.”
items.title: Habenula
items.description: Small bilateral neuronal structure in the brain of vertebrates
items.extract: The habenula is a small bilateral neuronal structure in the brain of vertebrates, that has also been called a microstructure since it is no bigger than a pea. The naming as "little rein" describes its elongated shape in the epithalamus, where it borders the third ventricle, and lies in front of the pineal gland.

prompts.text: Name a region of the world that spans multiple countries (like the Middle East)

items.quip: Chernobyl's exclusion zone lies inside this vast marshy forest region.
items.title: Polesia
items.description: Natural and historical region of Eastern Europe
items.extract: Polesia, also called Palessie, Polissia or Polesie, is a natural (geographic) and historical region in Eastern Europe within the East European Plain, including the Belarus–Ukraine border region and part of eastern Poland. This region should not be confused with parts of Russia also traditionally called "Polesie".

items.title: Oden
items.extract: Oden is a type of nabemono consisting of several ingredients such as boiled eggs, daikon or konjac, and processed fish balls stewed in a light, soy-flavored dashi broth.

prompts.text: Name a word of 3 or more letters you can spell with the letters in "krillion"

items.quip: A small Japanese medicine case worn hanging from a kimono sash.
items.title: Inro
items.extract: An inro  is a traditional Japanese case for holding small objects, suspended from the obi (sash) worn around the waist when wearing a kimono. They are often highly decorated with various materials such as lacquer and various techniques such as maki-e, and are more decorative than other Japanese lacquerware.
